correctness.rationale: The unital cubic-jet quotient A=K⊕V⊕Sym²V has no positive-degree cube. In characteristic ≠2, comparison of D²(ab) with D(ab) forces 2D(a)D(b)=0; images of all generators then have zero scalar and linear parts because squares of nonzero linear forms in Sym²V are nonzero, and idempotence forces D=0. In characteristic 2, cubic relations rule out constant generator images; every derivation D|V=P+Q with P:V→V and Q:V→Sym²V obeys D²=D exactly when P²=P and Q=QP+δ_P Q. Splitting V=imP⊕kerP yields Q(imP)⊂Sym²(imP)⊕Sym²(kerP), Q(kerP)⊂imP·kerP. Quadratic automorphism shear H=Q eliminates Q. Thus precisely n+1 orbits, full D rank r(n-r+1), and over even F_q number of rank-r operators is Gaussian(n,r,q) q^[r(n-r)+r(binomial(r+1,2)+binomial(n-r+1,2)+(n-r)^2)]. Independent enumeration for n=2,q=2 gives 1+112t²; n=3,q=2 symbolic count 1+269312t³+28672t⁴. Arbitrary-field result is established algebraically, not by these finite tests.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge novel is the exact classification and finite-field rank enumerator for the symmetric cubic maximal-ideal quotient, not the known idempotent-derivation/Z2-grading equivalence. The equivalent binary grading and a related but different truncated-coordinate algebra were inspected in primary sources. No located prior work logically implies this exact normal-form-plus-rank enumeration; unlocated more general graded Artin-algebra classification remains a real historical risk.
residual_risks: Possibly an unidentified general theorem classifies binary gradings of all cubic local Artin algebras and entails this classification.
A hidden prior finite-field rank table under algebra-gradings terminology cannot be ruled out.
Finite small-n checks are not proof of arbitrary-field assertions.

value.rationale: Composition-idempotent derivations are a natural form of Z2 grading; their automorphism classes and complete rank distribution are intrinsic, reusable invariants of the standard symmetric cubic local algebra in every dimension. The quadratic-shear dimensions vary with the projection rank; the result is not merely the standard count of matrix projections.
